title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. G is the dual graph (or 'Lego' graph) of a stable marked curve X. It has vertices s, edges A, half-edges or legs I, and oriented arcs \vec A_s at each vertex. Every vertex except a distinguished one, s_0, is a rigid pair of pants (three arcs). The component at s_0 is a genus-0 curve Y with |J| marked points, where J = \vec A_{s_0} is the set of arcs issuing from s_0. So Y varies in M_{0,J}, and X ranges over a boundary stratum of the Deligne-Mumford compactification isomorphic to M_{0,J}. In the notes this is used with |J| = 4, so the stratum is one-dimensional.

What SP_X is. It appears to be the set of 'standard base point' data attached to X: tangential, or smoothing-parameter, choices at the nodes and markings. The previous page shows it is a product SP_X = \prod_{a\in\hat A} T_a of one torsor T_a per edge or leg.
- Edges away from s_0: T_a is built from finite {\pm1}-data on the pants vertices (orderings and orientations of arcs). It does not depend on Y.
- Edges incident to s_0: T_a involves the tangent data T_i of Y at the marked point i \in J. There are three cases:
  - (I) a leg: T_a = T_i;
  - (II) a loop at s_0 with ends i, i': T_a = T_i \wedge T_{i'}. This is the familiar fact that the smoothing direction of a node is the tensor product of the two branch tangent lines;
  - (III) an edge from s_0 to a pants vertex s: T_a = T_i \wedge_{\{\pm1\}} (\hat A_s \setminus \{\vec a\}). Here the other end contributes a {\pm1}-torsor coming from the two remaining arcs at s.

This page. Let A_1 be the edges not touching s_0, and A_2 = A \setminus A_1 the edges incident to s_0 (the margin note says exactly this).
- The product splits as SP_X = T_{A_1} \times T^Y_J. Here T_{A_1} is the constant part, a disjoint union or contracted product of the \varepsilon_a over {\pm1}^{A_1}. T^Y_J = \prod_{a\in A_2} T_a; each factor is a product of at most two T_i's.
- The graph structure near s_0 induces a decomposition J = J_I \amalg J_{II} \amalg J_{III}:
  - J_I: arcs that are legs (marked points);
  - J_{II}: arcs that are ends of loops, with a fixed-point-free involution \sigma_{II} pairing the two ends of each loop;
  - J_{III}: arcs going to other vertices, equipped with a degree-2 covering \tilde J_{III} \to J_{III}, whose fibre over i is the two other arcs at the far vertex.
- Hence T^Y_J = T^Y_{J_I} \times T^Y_{J_{II}} \times T^Y_{J_{III}}. The next page writes these out explicitly and observes that, as Y varies, they become U-torsors on M_{0,J}. This gives SP_G \cong T_{\hat A_1} (a constant U^{A_1}-torsor) \times T_{A_2} (a U^{A_2}-torsor over M_{0,J}).

Purpose. To describe the action of the fundamental groupoid of the Teichmüller tower on well-chosen 'base points' at degenerate curves. The aim is presumably presenting the genus-0 and genus-1 Teichmüller groupoids by generators and relations, starting from the one-dimensional strata, whose orbifold points are examined on the next page.

Summary. The page is essentially bookkeeping: it splits the base-point torsor of a one-dimensional boundary stratum into a constant part and a part fibred over M_{0,J}, organized by the local combinatorics (legs / loops / edges to pants) at the non-rigid vertex.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The bookkeeping is consistent: each T_i with i in J occurs exactly once in T^Y_J; for a loop, the two ends occur together in a single factor T_i \wedge T_{i'}, which matches the remark on the previous page.

The indexing in the T_{A_1} formula is sloppy: \hat A_1 versus A_1, and \amalg versus contracted product over {\pm1}^{A_1}. The precise structure of T_{A_1} (disjoint union versus torsor) is left ambiguous on this page.
The phrase 'dépendant dans le cas des deux genres' and the remark about one or two loops at s_0 (genus 0 versus genus 1 one-dimensional strata) are only sketched.

ideas.what: Base-point torsor at a degenerate curve factors as a product over nodes and legs; the smoothing direction of a node is the product of the two branch tangent data (T_i \wedge T_{i'}).
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points / normal bundle to a boundary divisor of \bar M_{g,n} (N = T_p \otimes T_q)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne-Mumford (1969) for the deformation theory; Deligne (1989) for tangential base points; Ihara-Nakamura for Galois actions at maximal degenerations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of base points at 'points à l'infini' of the Teichmüller tower (only qualitatively)

ideas.what: Restricting the tangential base-point torsor to a 1-dimensional boundary stratum M_{0,J} (|J| = 4): a constant part from the rigid pants plus a U-torsor over M_{0,J} built from the tangent data at the marked points.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points along boundary strata; edges of the Lego-Teichmüller complex / 'moves' between maximally degenerate curves
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the 'jeu de Lego-Teichmüller' but without this explicit torsor computation

ideas.what: Combinatorial splitting J = J_I \amalg J_{II} \amalg J_{III} (legs; loop ends with a free involution; edges to pants with a double cover \tilde J_{III} \to J_{III}) and the corresponding product decomposition of the torsor.
ideas.modern_name: Local structure of a stable graph at a vertex (half-edges, loops, edges), as in Kontsevich-Manin / Getzler-Kapranov modular operads
ideas.usually_credited_to: Getzler-Kapranov (modular operads, 1998); stable graph formalism of Kontsevich-Manin

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an explicit description of the tangential base-point torsor SP_G over each one-dimensional stratum M_{0,J}, as constant {\pm1}-data times a U^{A_2}-torsor. He does this in order to compute the action of the Teichmüller fundamental groupoid on these base points, including at orbifold points of M_{0,4}. It is a detailed, unpublished preliminary to the Lego-Teichmüller generators-and-relations programme. The modern literature (Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura) reached analogous results independently, so this is a historical rather than a mathematical gap.
missed.quote: J = J_I \amalg J_{II} \amalg J_{III} ... J_{II} est muni d'une involution sans pts fixes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents how Grothendieck intended to handle base points and orbifold points in the Teichmüller tower. This is of interest for the history of the Lego-Teichmüller game and the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group, but it is unlikely to contain new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is careful but routine bookkeeping about tangential base points along a one-dimensional boundary stratum. The underlying ideas (smoothing direction as a product of branch tangents, decomposition by stable-graph combinatorics) are standard and were later developed independently. Its value is mainly historical, as documentation of the unpublished working-out behind the Esquisse's Lego-Teichmüller programme.
transcription_corrections: 'J=\vec{\vec{A}}_{s_0}' should read 'J = \vec A_{s_0}' (the set of arcs issuing from s_0); 'J_1 l'ens des orientés' is better read as 'J_1 l'ens des éléments de J = \vec A_{s_0} qui sont des arcs liés par boucles'.

The bracketed remark after T^Y_J reads roughly '(produit d'ens. munis ... au plus deux facteurs)', i.e. each factor T_a is a product of at most two T_i's. It is not 'unions dans objets au plus grandes facteurs'.
Line beginning '... J_{II} est muni': read 'où J_{II} est muni d'une involution sans pts fixes \sigma_{II}'.
'J_{III} est muni d'une ... de degré 2 J_{III}\to J_{III}' should read 'J_{III} est muni d'un revêtement de degré 2 \tilde J_{III} \to J_{III}', with the tilde over the source.
The last line reads approximately 'On a alors, en termes de [cette structure], T_J^Y = T^Y_{J_I} \times T^Y_{J_{II}} \times T^Y_{J_{III}}'.
Margin note: 'A \setminus A_1 = ens des arêtes incidentes à s_0' is correctly transcribed.
